column1: # Questions only a native speaker or Chinese teacher can settle. Each line: where
column3: the question

column2: 他不在房间里，在房间外。
column3: Is 房间外 natural, or would you say 房间外边 / 外面? (localizer 外 straight after a noun)
Is 学校前 natural here, or should this be 学校前面?
Is 学校后 natural here, or should this be 学校后面?
Is 桌子下 natural, or 桌子下面?
Is 玩电脑 natural for "play on the computer" (games, browsing), or is there a better verb?
Is 你的电话是多少 natural for "what's your phone number" without 号码?
Is 好玩儿 natural for a country, or is it mostly for things like games and activities?
Fine, but would a native speaker add a measure word or say 几本书 here?
Neutral tone: 这里 zhèli (as written) or zhèlǐ? Same for 那里 and 哪里.
Fine? (checking family-term style: 我哥哥 vs 我的哥哥)
Is 买些水果吧 natural as a standalone suggestion?
Is 一日 the right spoken form here, or 一号? (written/formal vs spoken)
I mean "it has started snowing / it is snowing today". Is 今天下雪了 natural for that, and does it risk reading as "it snowed earlier today"?
Is 你是对的 natural in speech, or do people say 你说得对 / 你对?
Is 一个电视 fine in speech, or should it be 一台电视?
Does 我上学时 mean "when I go to school (every day)" or "when I was a student"? Qwen says it leans to the second; is 我去上学的时候 clearer?
Is 我很疼 (no body part) odd? Qwen says yes; I replaced it with a headache sentence to be safe.
Is 手机保一年 natural for "the phone has a one-year warranty", or would a shop say 手机保修一年 / 保修期一年? (保 on its own as "to guarantee" before a time length)

column2: 池里有很多红色的小鱼。
column3: Is 池里 natural for "in the pond", or would people say 池子里 / 池塘里? (池 on its own)
The card teaches only the lively / energy sense (jīngshen). Is 他今天很有精神 the most natural example for it? The other sense, spirit (jīngshén), is only in the note: is the card balanced enough for HSK 5?
The card glosses 实力 as "strength; real ability". Is "capability" a better gloss, and is 这个队的实力很强 natural?

column2: 这个城市的人口增了很多。
column3: Is 增了 (on its own, without 加) natural in speech here, or would people say 增加了 / 多了? The card is a single-character entry.
Is 支 normal as the measure word for a team (一支球队) at this level, or do learners more often meet it only with pens (一支笔)?

column2: 他作出了一个重要的决定。
column3: Is 作出 natural here, or would a native speaker write 做出了一个重要的决定? Same for 作出了回答 and 作出了最大的努力.
Is 令人 + adjective (令人吃惊, 令人满意) natural in speech, or mainly in writing and the news? And is 他的话令我很感动 (令 + a named person) fine, or would you say 让我很感动 / 使我很感动?

column2: 今天够冷的，多穿一点吧。
column3: 够 + adjective + 的: the lesson says it shows surprise, sympathy or complaint ("quite cold, isn't it"). Is that the right description, and is 够冷的 natural for a simple comment on the weather?
将要 + verb: the lesson calls it formal and says it usually does not end with 了. Is that accurate? Is 将要 more common in news and announcements than in speech (where 快要 / 就要 is used)?
看你…的 ("look how tired you are"): is 看你累的 natural, and is the lesson right that 看你说的 can also mean "come on, don't say that" (a gentle complaint)?

column2: 什么钱不钱的，我们是朋友！
column3: 什么 + A + 不 + A + 的: is 什么钱不钱的 a natural way to wave something aside, and do people say it with other nouns (什么麻烦不麻烦的)?

column2: 我想来想去，还是决定去了。
column3: A来A去: is 想来想去 natural for "thinking it over and over", and does the lesson overstate it when it says the verb can be any verb that can repeat (走来走去, 找来找去, 说来说去)?
